The body generates heat in part from the muscles working.

In any given material, its strength properties for tension, compression, torsion, and flexure can be determined, and these properties are related to the stress-strain behavior of the material, or what stress (pressure) will induce a strain (total deformation/unit length). Work, is the energy required for some force to displace something. Since deformation falls into the same category as displacement (when something is stretched its constituent atoms are displaced from their original position), deformation similarly is a form of work. So when something deforms, work is performed due to the strain within the material deforming.

This behavior is best modeled by elastic spring behavior.

Since muscles are little more than bundles of elastic fibers, they are effectively springs which stretch and compress. When they stretch and compress, they convert energy and perform work. When work is performed, heat is generated (by strain, friction, etc). That is part of why you generate heat when you exercise.
